items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The row's parenthetical Hebrew for web:Job.6.21 is the ENTIRE verse and collates BYTE at oshb:Job.6.21 (כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם לא ל֑וֹ תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ); the staged extract carries the ketiv and the qere ADJACENT at tokens 4-5 of that verse, לא ל֑וֹ (ketiv unpointed, qere pointed), and pmarks_Job.json kq registers 1 note at Job.6.21 (book: 49 kq verses, flagged HIGH). The quoted run therefore CROSSES the ketiv/qere adjacency, the canonical disclosure trigger (strategy section 4 and section 2e-b: disclose when a quoted span crosses the adjacency; TOOLKIT wording governs), and the shipped row carries no ketiv, qere or K/Q disclosure anywhere in boundary_rationale, boundary_evidence_refs or strongest_rejected_alternative (search of the shipped fields: zero hits). The quote is not byte-false, so the defect is exactly the class filed: two readings of one word are presented silently as continuous verse text. The gloss arm is weaker than filed: 'all second-person plural' reads naturally as a description of the finite verbs, and those three ARE 2mp (הֱיִ֣יתֶם qatal, תִּֽרְא֥וּ yiqtol, וַתִּירָֽאוּ wayyiqtol), while כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה, the ketiv/qere pair and the noun חֲ֝תַ֗ת are not verbs; narrowing the gloss to the verbs is a tidy repair, not an added defect. Severity holds at medium, not high: 6:21 is the onset of the disclosed INTERNAL rival, not a row edge; the near edge stands in oshb:Job.6.14 (לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב: 3ms suffix on מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ, 3ms yiqtol יַעֲזֽוֹב) after the 1cs close of oshb:Job.6.13 (עֶזְרָתִ֣י בִ֑י, מִמֶּֽנִּי), and the far edge in the 2mp imperative opening oshb:Job.6.24 (ה֭וֹרוּנִי) after the 2mp yiqtol close of oshb:Job.6.23 (תִּפְדּֽוּנִי); neither rests on 6:21. Not low: an undisclosed crossing inside a quoted span is a quote-integrity, mark-class defect named in the calibration law, not a missing label on a true claim. Repair proposal validated against the same bytes: disclosing the crossing inside the oshb:Job.6.21 parenthetical (WLC single-witness; ketiv and qere adjacent in the extract) and narrowing the person gloss to the three finite verbs is exact; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only, span, edges and the low band untouched. both_sides_assessed is false because the item concerns no seam (a K/Q quote-parity item). Out-of-scope observation for owner triage only: the same undisclosed-crossing class recurs at oshb:Job.6.29 (kq 1, tokens ושבי וְשׁ֥וּבוּ) inside the adjacent unit's full-verse quote.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. Arithmetic: the rejected merge is Job.7.11-Job.7.21 = 11 verses (6 + 5), INSIDE strategy section 6's '~4-12 vv guide' for a strophe-level row, so 'past a comfortable strophe length' is false against the book's own band; and section 6 rules that rows are 'seamed at tier-1 signals ONLY' and treats row comparability as a convergence constraint, not evidence (the auditor's paraphrase lifts that phrase from section 6's chapter-scale sentence, but the conclusion is unchanged), so length cannot carry a rival's rejection in any case. The seam itself re-derives sound from both sides: the preceding unit closes at oshb:Job.7.16 in 1cs self-reference, מָ֭אַסְתִּי לֹא לְעֹלָ֣ם אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה חֲדַ֥ל מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי כִּי הֶ֥בֶל יָמָֽי (1cs qatal מָ֭אַסְתִּי, 1cs suffixes on מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי and יָמָֽי), and the row opens at oshb:Job.7.17 on the verse-initial topic-turn interrogative מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ (collates BYTE at its cited ref; מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ pivots from Job's own life-loathing to the what-is-man question put to God), a tier-1 class in section 6's list; the preceding unit names the same edge ('ending before the next topic-turn interrogative'), so the adjacent rows argue the shared seam coherently. The far edge is likewise byte-grounded: oshb:Job.7.21 (וּמֶ֤ה לֹא תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ וְתַעֲבִ֪יר אֶת עֲוֺ֫נִ֥י כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה לֶעָפָ֣ר אֶשְׁכָּ֑ב וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי) is followed by PE (pmarks_Job.json marks[Job.7.21] = PE, single-witness, tier-3) and oshb:Job.8.1 opens Bildad's formula וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר. What fails is only the rival's STATED ground: a defective warrant that is not load-bearing because the seam's tier-1 warrant stands in the row's own rationale (not high); not low because a rival rejection resting solely on a false, non-evidence ground is a warrant defect, not a register slip. Repair proposal validated: re-grounding the rejection on the tier-1 interrogative opening oshb:Job.7.17 (already in the refs) and deleting the length assertion is supported by the bytes above; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only, no span change. both_sides_assessed true (7:16 close and 7:17 onset weighed under the topic-turn rule; the speaker-change far edge weighed as well).

Re-derived from bytes both ways. sweep.py --web 'umpire' returns 1 verse book-wide, Job.9.33: “There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.” web:Job.9.33 (Hebrew לֹ֣א יֵשׁ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ מוֹכִ֑יחַ יָשֵׁ֖ת יָד֣וֹ עַל שְׁנֵֽינוּ, the מוֹכִ֑יחַ 'arbiter' line); sweeps for 'arbiter' (0), 'mediator' (0) and 'between us' (1, Job.9.33) add no verse inside chapter 7. That verse lies outside the span, outside chapter 7 and inside Job's reply to Bildad, with its companion oshb:Job.9.32 (נָב֥וֹא יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט, 'come together in judgment') also in chapter 9. The span's own bytes carry no arbiter, umpire or mediator: oshb:Job.7.17 מָֽה אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ (what-is-man interrogative), oshb:Job.7.18 וַתִּפְקְדֶ֥נּוּ לִבְקָרִ֑ים לִ֝רְגָעִ֗ים תִּבְחָנֶֽנּוּ (morning-by-morning visitation and testing), oshb:Job.7.19 opening כַּ֭מָּה (how long), oshb:Job.7.20 with נֹצֵ֪ר הָאָ֫דָ֥ם ('watcher of men') and לְמִפְגָּ֣ע ('as a mark'), and oshb:Job.7.21 opening וּמֶ֤ה לֹא תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ (the pardon question) and closing וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי. The shipped label 'divine arbitration impossibility: no umpire between Job and God' therefore describes material that stands nowhere in Job.7.17-Job.7.21: byte-false for the span. Medium is right: a byte-false content descriptor is a defective claim in a graph-facing field, but it bears on neither edge and is not load-bearing (not high), and it is not a mechanical or register slip (not low). The row's mark cites re-verify: pmarks_Job.json marks[Job.7.21] = PE, paseq[Job.7.20] = 1, paseq[Job.7.21] = 1, cited count-only with no intra-verse position claim and labelled single-witness and corroborating. Repair proposal validated: the suggested label 'closing plea: divine scrutiny of man and the unanswered request for pardon' matches the span's bytes (scrutiny 7:17-18, how-long and watcher 7:19-20, pardon question 7:21); endorsed with the qualification that any label drawn from the span satisfies the repair, a PROPOSAL only, no span, ref or confidence change. both_sides_assessed false: a content-label item that concerns no seam.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json: oshb:Job.9.22 word 6 is תָּ֥ם (codepoints TAV, DAGESH, QAMATS, U+05A5 MERKHA, FINAL MEM), while oshb:Job.9.20 word 5 and oshb:Job.9.21 word 1 are both תָּֽם (TAV, DAGESH, QAMATS, U+05BD METEG, FINAL MEM). collate.py: the 9:22 token against oshb:Job.9.20 and against oshb:Job.9.21 returns tier SKELETON in both cases (nfd and accent_stripped also fail, because the staged extract strips the merkha but RETAINS meteg); the 9:20 token against oshb:Job.9.21 returns BYTE. So the two tokens closing the preceding strophe are byte-identical to each other ('twice' is true), and the 9:22 token matches them only at skeleton tier: the shipped 'repeats - at byte tier -' is a tier overclaim (E-05), which the row's own prose exposes by displaying the two distinct pointed forms side by side. The bond is real at skeleton tier, so the row's cross-seam corroboration and its medium_low band survive with the tier corrected; the row itself frames the bond as disclosed corroboration that moves neither strophe's edge, so it is not load-bearing (not high), and a false tier label on a quoted identity is a defective claim rather than a register slip (not low): medium confirmed. Repair proposal validated: 'repeats at SKELETON tier (distinct pointed forms: merkha at 9:22, meteg at 9:20 and 9:21, which are byte-identical to each other)' states exactly the codepoint facts above; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed false: a tier/count-object item; the 9:21|9:22 seam is not moved by it.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. oshb:Job.9.23 reads אִם שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג: word 5 לְמַסַּ֖ת is a construct noun ('at the trial of'), word 6 נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', its nomen rectum, and word 7 יִלְעָֽג, the verse-final word, is the 3ms yiqtol 'he mocks'; WEB “If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.” web:Job.9.23. The shipped sentence splices נְקִיִּ֣ם and glosses it 'mocks' while arguing that it 'has no expressed subject of its own', a predication that is true of the verb יִלְעָֽג and impossible for a noun inside a construct chain. The splice is byte-valid (collates BYTE at oshb:Job.9.23) but names the wrong word for the claim: a wrong-token splice as filed. The underlying continuity observation survives with the right token (the explicit 3ms subject ה֣וּא of מְכַלֶּֽה at oshb:Job.9.22 carries over to the subjectless יִלְעָֽג), so the row's edges and band are untouched: not load-bearing (not high), and a semantically wrong quoted word is a defective warrant rather than a mechanical slip (not low): medium confirmed. Repair proposal validated: swapping the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, matches the bytes; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns an intra-row token, not a seam.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. The adjacent preceding unit spans Job.16.9-Job.16.14 (six verses); its opening verse oshb:Job.16.9 begins אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide; a 3ms-suffixed subject noun fronted before its 3ms qatal verb, Job the 1cs object in וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֵ֗נִי), whereas שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי is byte-exact at oshb:Job.16.12 only (sweep.py --heb: byte 1, skeleton 1) and Job.16.12 is that unit's FOURTH verse. The shipped locator 'the preceding row's own opening ... Job.16.12' is therefore false as a cross-row claim (E-18 arm), while the point it serves (fronting is ambient in the preceding unit, hence non-distinctive as an edge signal) is true at the real opening. The same verse softens the row's role contrast, as the auditor says: הָיִ֨יתִי is a 1cs qatal inside the range the row describes as holding Job as object. Both sides of the seam re-derive sound under the book's participant-shift rule: oshb:Job.16.14 closes יִפְרְצֵ֣נִי פֶ֭רֶץ עַל פְּנֵי פָ֑רֶץ יָרֻ֖ץ עָלַ֣י כְּגִבּֽוֹר (3ms verbs, Job the 1cs object in יִפְרְצֵ֣נִי and עָלַ֣י), and oshb:Job.16.15 opens שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי בֶעָפָ֣ר קַרְנִֽי (fronted object plus 1cs qatal תָּ֭פַרְתִּי, then 1cs וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי); the preceding unit names the same edge ('gives way to Job's own self-description of mourning at 16:15'), so the adjacent rows are coherent, and the far edge at oshb:Job.16.18 (אֶ֭רֶץ אַל תְּכַסִּ֣י, vocative plus 2fs jussive) is argued identically by the following unit. pmarks_Job.json records no PE or SAMEKH in chapter 16 (absence is not counterevidence). The defect is thus a false cross-row locator that is not load-bearing: medium confirmed (not high; not low because the claim is false, not merely workflow-phrased). Repair proposal validated: 'the preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף, oshb:Job.16.9), as does Job.16.12 inside it' matches the bytes, and adding oshb:Job.16.9 to boundary_evidence_refs anchors it; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL with one qualification: the wording should be verse-anchored rather than positional ('the unit opening at Job.16.9') to satisfy section 10's register purge. both_sides_assessed true.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. The adjacent preceding unit spans Job.21.27-Job.21.34 and closes at oshb:Job.21.34, וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם נִשְׁאַר מָֽעַל, a 2mp address to the friends (תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי, וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם) followed by SAMEKH (pmarks_Job.json marks[Job.21.34] = SAMEKH, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only); oshb:Job.21.1, וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, collates BYTE and is one of the nine book-wide members of the generic Job-reply formula (byte sweep: 9 verses), standing 26 verses before that unit's first verse as the opening of Job's speech, not any unit's close. The row opens at oshb:Job.22.1 on the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (BYTE, sole book-wide hit), so the seam is Job.21.34|Job.22.1 under the explicit speaker-change rule, with the SAMEKH corroborating; the adjacent unit argues the same seam ('immediately before Eliphaz's third-speech formula opens at 22:1'), so the two rows are coherent. The shipped sentence is false twice over: 'the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1)' misdescribes the adjacent unit's close (E-18 arm), and 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1' pairs verses 34 apart in the pipe notation this corpus uses for adjacent verses (the slice's own rows write Job.6.20|Job.6.21, Job.9.27|Job.9.28, 6:23|6:24). The seam and its warrant are unaffected, so the defect is not load-bearing (not high), and a byte-false cross-row claim is more than a register slip (not low): medium confirmed. Repair proposal validated: 'The speaker-change seam at Job.21.34|Job.22.1 opens this row: Job's speech, opened by וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.21.1, ends at Job.21.34, and this row opens with Eliphaz answering, וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.22.1)' matches the bytes above, the speech-end claim resting on the 22:1 formula with the SAMEKH as tier-3 corroboration; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed true.

Re-derived from bytes: the first word of every verse of Eliphaz's third speech, oshb:Job.22.2-Job.22.30, read from verse_map_oshb.json (count object: verse-initial interrogative he, exhaustive over the 29 verses). Members: Job.22.2 הַלְאֵ֥ל, Job.22.3 הַחֵ֣פֶץ, Job.22.4 הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ, Job.22.5 הֲלֹ֣א, Job.22.12 הֲֽלֹא, Job.22.15 הַאֹ֣רַח: six. The only other he-initial verses are correctly non-members: Job.22.17 הָאֹמְרִ֣ים carries the qamats article on a participle, and Job.22.21 הַסְכֶּן is a hiphil imperative (WEB renders it as the imperative 'Acquaint yourself with him now'); no verse from 22:16 to 22:30 opens on a further interrogative he. Job.22.15 is interrogative in form (patah he before aleph, where the article would take qamats) and in rendering, “Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,” web:Job.22.15. So Job.22.12 is correctly the FIFTH member but 'final' is byte-false: a false exclusivity claim (E-05). Not load-bearing (the claim sits beyond the row's far edge; the opening seam rests on the formula at oshb:Job.22.1 and the far-edge rejection on הֲלֹ֣א at oshb:Job.22.5 and the connectives כִּֽי, וְאִ֣ישׁ, אוֹ), so not high; a false digit-class claim is not a mere disclosure gap, so not low: medium confirmed. The row's other digits in the same field re-derive TRUE with their objects named: הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י byte sweep 1 (Job.22.1; skeleton 1), הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י byte sweep 2 (Job.4.1, Job.15.1) and skeleton sweep 5 (Job.2.11, Job.4.1, Job.15.1, Job.42.7, Job.42.9), so the row's '5 times book-wide' is a spelling-level count, matching WEB 'Temanite' 6 verses = 5 + 1. Repair proposal validated: 'Eliphaz's fifth ha-interrogative falls outside this row at Job.22.12, and a sixth and final one opens Job.22.15 (הַאֹ֣רַח, oshb:Job.22.15)' is exact against the exhaustive sweep; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed false: a count-object item that concerns no seam.
